identity_scope: 442 AIO records including all scoped synonyms and 44 existing native records were compared. Ignored-inclusive textual hits were prior pending leads, reviews and Adam variant notes, not duplicate identities. A broad adaptive-subgradient alias was searched but not asserted for diagonal Adagrad.

entries.name: AdamW
entries.identity_assessment: Decoupled weight decay distinguishes AdamW from Adam with a penalty included in its gradient moments. It is an optimization algorithm, not a new model architecture.
entries.inspected_method: Parameters receive a weight-decay shrinkage step, while first and second gradient moments are updated from the objective gradient and used for the adaptive step.
entries.source_interpretation: Versioned official implementation documentation, not an abstract or an experimental comparison.
limitations: The cited implementation also offers an optional AMSGrad variant; that option is not required by the AdamW definition.
No universal convergence or performance advantage is asserted.

entries.name: Adagrad
entries.identity_assessment: This record covers the commonly implemented diagonal Adagrad algorithm. Its cumulative accumulator differs from the exponentially decayed squared-gradient estimate in RMSprop.
entries.inspected_method: The diagonal variant accumulates squared gradients over iterations and divides the current gradient by the square root of that accumulator plus a numerical stabilizer.
entries.source_interpretation: Versioned official implementation documentation, not an abstract or an experimental comparison.
limitations: The definition is scoped to the inspected diagonal implementation, not every full-matrix adaptive subgradient formulation.
Initialization, learning-rate decay and regularization settings are implementation choices; no benchmark or convergence claim is made.

entries.name: RMSprop
entries.locator: RMSprop.__doc__, algorithm and implementation note lines 200–243
entries.identity_assessment: RMSprop decays older squared-gradient information, unlike cumulative Adagrad. Centered and momentum settings are variants within this scoped record.
entries.inspected_method: An exponential moving average of squared gradients supplies the update denominator; the documented centered option subtracts a squared mean-gradient estimate, and momentum is optional.
entries.source_interpretation: Versioned official implementation documentation, not an abstract or an experimental comparison.
limitations: The cited implementation adds epsilon after the square root and documents a different ordering in TensorFlow.
No universal improvement or convergence guarantee is inferred from implementation documentation.

entries.name: Adadelta
entries.identity_assessment: The additional update-history scale distinguishes Adadelta from RMSprop and from Adagrad's cumulative accumulator.
entries.inspected_method: The update multiplies the gradient by the stabilized root-mean-square of prior updates divided by the stabilized root-mean-square of current gradient history, then updates the squared-update average.
entries.source_interpretation: Versioned official implementation documentation, not an abstract or an experimental comparison.
limitations: The inspected implementation includes a learning-rate multiplier; this record does not describe it as parameter-free.
No convergence theorem or comparative benchmark result is curated.

entries.name: Adafactor
entries.locator: Adafactor.__doc__, algorithm lines 178–224 and implementation differences lines 229–285
entries.identity_assessment: Adafactor factors the adaptive second-moment state; it is not low-rank adaptation of model weights such as LoRA. Vector parameters use an unfactored second-moment estimate.
entries.inspected_method: For matrix parameters, row and column statistics reconstruct a factored second-moment estimate used to normalize gradients; the inspected implementation also clips update RMS and scales steps using parameter RMS.
entries.source_interpretation: Versioned official implementation documentation, not an abstract or an experimental comparison.
limitations: PyTorch documents differences from the original paper in learning-rate control and epsilon handling; the record does not equate their exact update equations.
No measured memory reduction, benchmark superiority or convergence guarantee is asserted.

entries.name: AdaMax
entries.identity_assessment: AdaMax changes Adam's normalization statistic and is retained as a distinct algorithm; it is not an alias for Adam.
entries.inspected_method: The first-moment estimate is bias-corrected, while the denominator takes the coordinatewise maximum of the decayed prior scale and the current absolute gradient with the implementation's stabilizer.
entries.source_interpretation: Versioned official implementation documentation, not an abstract or an experimental comparison.
limitations: Epsilon placement follows the cited PyTorch implementation.
No universal convergence or benchmark advantage is asserted.

entries.name: NAdam
entries.locator: NAdam.__doc__, algorithm lines 214–252 and options lines 257–266
entries.identity_assessment: The Nesterov-style combination distinguishes NAdam from Adam. Optional decoupled weight decay is not required for this identity.
entries.inspected_method: The documented update combines a scheduled, bias-adjusted first-moment term with a current-gradient term and divides the combination by a stabilized, bias-corrected second-moment scale.
entries.source_interpretation: Versioned official implementation documentation, not an abstract or an experimental comparison.
limitations: The source specifies a momentum schedule and an optional NAdamW configuration; other implementations need separate exact-equation comparison.
No comparative performance or convergence claim is curated.

entries.name: Rectified Adam
entries.locator: RAdam.__doc__, algorithm lines 176–218 and weight-decay note lines 220–225
entries.identity_assessment: RAdam's rectification and early-step branch distinguish it from unmodified Adam and from weight-decay decoupling alone.
entries.inspected_method: The cited implementation computes a rectification term when its effective-history statistic exceeds five; before that threshold it takes a bias-corrected first-moment step without adaptive second-moment scaling.
entries.source_interpretation: Versioned official implementation documentation, not an abstract or an experimental comparison.
limitations: The implementation exposes coupled and decoupled weight-decay choices; these are distinct from the rectification mechanism.
The record asserts the update procedure, not a universal variance reduction, convergence result or benchmark advantage.

entries.name: Averaged stochastic gradient descent
entries.locator: ASGD class documentation lines 174–200 and _single_tensor_asgd averaging/update lines 248–273
entries.identity_assessment: ASGD adds parameter-iterate averaging to stochastic gradient descent. It is not the same operation as averaging gradients in a momentum buffer.
entries.inspected_method: The inspected implementation updates the current parameters by a scheduled gradient step and maintains an auxiliary parameter average, with averaging weights controlled by the iteration count and a configurable starting point.
entries.source_interpretation: Versioned official implementation documentation, not an abstract or an experimental comparison.
limitations: This record covers iterate averaging in the cited ASGD implementation, not every stochastic weight averaging schedule.
No convergence rate or generalization advantage is asserted.

entries.name: Limited-memory BFGS
entries.locator: LBFGS class documentation lines 183–220 and step curvature-history/two-loop update lines 360–408
entries.identity_assessment: L-BFGS is an optimization algorithm, not a neural architecture; bounded curvature history distinguishes it from full-memory BFGS.
entries.inspected_method: The implementation retains a bounded set of curvature pairs and applies a two-loop recursion to obtain a direction from the gradient without storing a dense inverse Hessian.
entries.source_interpretation: Versioned official implementation documentation, not an abstract or an experimental comparison.
limitations: The cited implementation imposes parameter-group and device restrictions that are not mathematical requirements of every L-BFGS implementation.
Line-search choices and termination tolerances affect a particular run; no universal convergence or speed guarantee is curated.

entries.name: Resilient backpropagation
entries.identity_assessment: Rprop is an optimizer using backpropagated gradients, not the backpropagation procedure for computing those gradients. Update magnitude is controlled by step size rather than current gradient magnitude.
entries.inspected_method: Repeated gradient signs increase a coordinate's bounded step size, while a sign reversal decreases it; in the cited variant the reversal also suppresses that coordinate's current update.
entries.source_interpretation: Versioned official implementation documentation, not an abstract or an experimental comparison.
limitations: Sign-reversal handling is scoped to the inspected PyTorch variant; other Rprop variants require comparison.
No comparative speed or convergence claim is asserted.

entries.name: Muon optimizer
entries.locator: Muon.__doc__, algorithm and orthogonalization lines 207–260; supported-parameter note lines 264–265
entries.identity_assessment: Muon is a matrix-update optimizer distinct from coordinatewise Adam-family scaling. The name here denotes the optimization algorithm, not unrelated uses of the word muon.
entries.inspected_method: The inspected implementation forms a momentum update, optionally uses a Nesterov combination, applies iterative matrix orthogonalization, and scales the resulting update for the parameter shape while applying decoupled weight decay.
entries.source_interpretation: Versioned official implementation documentation, not an abstract or an experimental comparison.
limitations: The cited implementation is scoped to two-dimensional hidden-layer parameters and directs other parameters to a standard optimizer.
The implementation provides alternative shape-scaling conventions; no universal exact orthogonality, convergence or performance guarantee is asserted.
